f.title: Definition: medically important event or reaction
f.statement: A medically important event or reaction is a clinical manifestation or adverse occurrence that, in medical or scientific judgement, is not immediately life-threatening, does not cause death or hospitalisation, but could endanger the patient or consumer or require medical intervention to prevent one of the seriousness criteria.
f.applicability: Draft PROY-NOM-220-SSA1-2024 (consultation draft, not in force).

f.title: Classify seriousness using the six criteria, including medically important events
f.statement: A case is serious when, with any dose of a medicine or vaccine, it causes death, is life-threatening when it occurs, requires or prolongs hospitalisation, causes disability or permanent or significant incapacity, causes alterations or malformations in the newborn, or is another important medical condition. Cases not meeting these criteria are non-serious.
